title: Claims Manual, Harbison Protection Contracts: Appeals on a Decided Claim
content:
### 1. Who may appeal and how often

A denied or partially approved claim on a Harbison Protection Contracts contract may be decided again on appeal, at most the tier's appeals-per-claim figure per claim, recorded as decision round 2. Whether a claim already has an appeal is read from its claim history: a decision in round 2 on that claim.

### 2. Appeal window

An appeal is decided only when the date of handling is no later than the tier's appeal window, in calendar days, after the original decision was posted. Appeal-window days are counted as calendar days with the original decision date as day 0, and an appeal decided on the last day is accepted. The original decision date is the date on the claim's round-1 decision entry.

Boundary case (hypothetical, 30-day window): original decision posted 3 March 2026 (day 0); day 30 is 2 April 2026. An appeal decided on 2 April 2026 is accepted; one on 3 April 2026 is not.

### 3. What the appeal looks at

An appeal is decided on the same tests as the original decision, using the records as they stand on the appeal date. A maintenance visit or a manufacturer registration that existed before the failure but was missed in the original decision can change the outcome; maintenance performed after the failure date never can.

### 4. What cannot change on appeal

A denial for a failure outside the coverage term, a component not covered, or an excluded cause cannot be overturned by new documents and is upheld on appeal.

### 5. Paying an appeal

When the appeal approves more than the original decision, only the difference is paid out, under the payout components not already paid. An appeal never reduces an amount already paid.

**Points of judgement (hypothetical).**

| Original outcome | New material on the appeal date | Appeal outcome |
|---|---|---|
| denied, maintenance not documented | a completed Comfort Club tune-up before the failure, missed at the original decision | decided again on the same tests; the maintenance test can now pass |
| denied, maintenance not documented | a tune-up performed after the failure date | cannot change the outcome |
| denied, component not covered | any document | upheld |
| approved for $600.00, appeal approves $750.00 | — | $150.00 paid out under components not already paid |
